newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps drift sideways with no lead from OP.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps drift sideways with no lead from OP.

text.p: European oil swaps drifted sideways in a directionless market that was thinning out activity.
Attention was focused on Vienna where OPEC was meeting, but the attention was barely warranted, said some traders.
"It doesn't look like anything new or anything unexpected will happen," said one.
Brent CFDs lost a few cents while fuel swaps held steady. Gasoline ticked up 50 cents while naphtha gained up to $3 for September contracts.

Brent CFDs saw June 30-July 4 ease a touch to -40 cents from -35/36 cents on Tuesday while July 7-11 slipped to -40 cents from -36/37 cents. Further out July 14-18 was broadly steady around -36 cents from -35 cents and July 21-25 was pegged at -33 cents from -30 cents.
July 7-11 traded twice against August 4-8 at -12 cents, dealers said.
Gas oil crack spreads heard talk, but no deals were seen. Fourth quarter was pegged at $4.45, Q198 at $4.55-4.65 and Q298 at $4.05-4.15.

Heavy fuel flitted around the $82.00 level for much of the day. In the morning there was a wide bid-offer spread with buyers looking for $81.50. By the afternoon dealers said the level was closer to $82.25 on the bid and $82.75/83.00 on the offer.
Gasoline swaps firmed by about 50 cents across the board with July, August and September all flat at $179.00.
Naphtha swaps saw the contango widen as the months progress. July edged up $1 to $174 from $173, while August moved to $175.50 and September was assessed at $178.
